https://www.itv.com/news/central/2025-04.title: Angela Rayner will continue to 'press all parties involved' to end Birmingham bin strikes
https://www.itv.com/news/central/2025-04.text:
Deputy Prime Minister Angela Rayner and top ministers will continue "press all parties involved" to end the bin strikes in Birmingham, the government has said.
Rayner met with Birmingham City Council leaders on Saturday night to discuss how to help "clear the waste backlog", as Unite union bin workers are on an indefinite strike over pay, conditions and job security.
The council declared a major incident on Monday, 31 March, to address the public health and environmental impact, as piles of waste were uncollected across the city.
Following Saturday's meeting, Minister of State for Local Government and English Devolution, Jim McMahon OBE said: “Our first and foremost priority continues to be the residents of Birmingham – to bring this disruption to an end and accelerate the clean up of their streets.
“Myself and the Deputy Prime Minister will continue to engage closely with the council on action they are taking to rapidly improve the situation on the ground and press all parties involved to get around the table and come to a resolution.”
Birmingham City Council Leader Cllr John Cotton said: “I am grateful for the continued support from central Government and local partners in the city.
"We were able to get crews out today (Sunday) and will continue to do all we can to clear the rubbish. I thank residents for their patience and staff for working hard to continue the service.”
A Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government spokesperson said Birmingham council has tried to mitigate the impact of the strikes by running collections over the weekend.
On Friday, Number 10 told Unite to “drop their opposition” to the pay changes at the heart of the dispute with the council.

https://www.itv.com/news/calendar/2025-0.title: Murder arrests after man's unexplained death in Doncaster
https://www.itv.com/news/calendar/2025-0.text:
Two people have been arrested on suspicion of murder after an "unexplained" death in Doncaster.
Police were called to Orchard Street in the Thorne area on Tuesday night after a 47-year-old man was found unresponsive.
He died at the scene.
A 38-year-old man and a 42-year-old woman have been arrested on suspicion of murder.
Det Ch Insp Simon Cartwright, of South Yorkshire Police, said: "We are in the early stages of the investigation. At this time the man's cause of death is unexplained and our team of detectives are working hard to establish the circumstances surrounding this incident."
He appealed for anyone with information to come forward.

https://www.itv.com/news/calendar/2025-0.title: Woman arrested after Knaresborough pub destroyed in major fire
https://www.itv.com/news/calendar/2025-0.text:
A woman has been arrested after a North Yorkshire pub was almost completely destroyed by a large fire.
The Cricketers, in Calcutt, near Knaresborough, went up in flames in the early hours of Tuesday, 1 April.
No one was injured, but the fire service said there had been "100% fire damage to the building".
North Yorkshire Police believe the fire was started deliberately. A woman has been arrested on suspicion of arson and remains in police custody
Crews from Knaresborough, Harrogate, Acomb, Tadcaster, Ripon and Wetherby were called to deal with the incident.
A spokesperson for Knaresborough Town council said: "Our thoughts are with all those affected, and the emergency services who have been responding to the fire.
"Please allow plenty of time and pick your route when out and about on the roads this morning as the fire may cause disruption."
